intro.title: Child processes
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Node.js application that uses child processes to run external commands, like listing directory contents, from within your JavaScript code. You will learn the core concept of spawning separate processes to execute system commands or other scripts, allowing your main program to continue running or handle the output. The main technologies involved are the Node.js `child_process` module and its methods such as `exec`. By the end, you'll understand how to safely run and interact with external processes in a Node.js environment.
intro.usecase: Child processes are essential in Node.js for offloading heavy tasks to keep your main application responsive. For example, a web dashboard that processes large CSV uploads or generates PDF reports uses child processes to run these intensive operations in the background. This pattern also powers features like real-time data processing in analytics tools or executing system commands in DevOps automation scripts, ensuring the primary UI remains fast and interactive.
